_about: Limitation rules as data for app/services/limitation_service.py. Prepared by engineering from the statute text. Every rule ships as a DRAFT: it applies in a firm only once two of that firm's members have signed its current version (rule_verifications, migration 014). Bump `version` whenever a rule's substance changes; sign-offs are per version. Schedule articles are cited as 'Article N of the Schedule to the Limitation Act, 1963'.

rules.title: Appeal to a High Court from a decree or order (CPC)
rules.basis: Article 116 of the Schedule to the Limitation Act, 1963 (clause (a)): appeal under the Code of Civil Procedure to a High Court from any decree or order, ninety days from the date of the decree or order. Appeals under Sections 96, 100 and 104 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. Computed under Sections 4, 5 and 12 of the Limitation Act, 1963.
rules.remedy: Appeal (first or second appeal, or appeal from an order)
rules.start_event: Date of the decree or order appealed from
rules.notes: Delay may be condoned on sufficient cause (s. 5); the condonation is for the court.

rules.title: Appeal to a court other than a High Court from a decree or order (CPC)
rules.basis: Article 116 of the Schedule to the Limitation Act, 1963 (clause (b)): appeal under the Code of Civil Procedure to any other court from any decree or order, thirty days from the date of the decree or order. Appeals under Sections 96 and 104 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. Computed under Sections 4, 5 and 12 of the Limitation Act, 1963.
rules.remedy: Appeal (first appeal or appeal from an order)
rules.forum: District court or other appellate court
rules.start_event: Date of the decree or order appealed from
rules.notes: Delay may be condoned on sufficient cause (s. 5).

rules.title: Intra-court appeal from a High Court decree or order to the same High Court
rules.basis: Article 117 of the Schedule to the Limitation Act, 1963: appeal from a decree or order of any High Court to the same Court, thirty days from the date of the decree or order. Computed under Sections 4, 5 and 12 of the Limitation Act, 1963.
rules.remedy: Intra-court appeal (Letters Patent appeal / appeal to a Division Bench)
rules.start_event: Date of the decree or order appealed from
rules.notes: Check the High Court's own rules for the appeal: a special statute or the court's rules may prescribe a different period.

rules.title: Review of a judgment (court other than the Supreme Court)
rules.basis: Article 124 of the Schedule to the Limitation Act, 1963: review of judgment by a court other than the Supreme Court, thirty days from the date of the decree or order. Section 114 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 and Order XLVII. Computed under Sections 4, 5 and 12 of the Limitation Act, 1963.
rules.forum: The court that passed the decree or order
rules.start_event: Date of the decree or order sought to be reviewed
rules.notes: A review is an application: s. 14(2) can apply to time spent in another proceeding with due diligence.

rules.title: Civil revision
rules.basis: Article 131 of the Schedule to the Limitation Act, 1963: to any court for the exercise of its powers of revision under the Code of Civil Procedure, ninety days from the date of the decree or order sought to be revised. Section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. Computed under Sections 4, 5, 12 and 14 of the Limitation Act, 1963.
rules.start_event: Date of the decree or order sought to be revised
rules.notes: Criminal revisions are not covered by this rule.

rules.title: Special leave petition (civil) to the Supreme Court
rules.basis: Article 133 of the Schedule to the Limitation Act, 1963 (clause (c)): special leave to appeal to the Supreme Court in any other case, ninety days from the date of the judgment or order. Order XXI Rule 1 of the Supreme Court Rules, 2013. Article 136 of the Constitution of India. Computed under Sections 4, 5 and 12 of the Limitation Act, 1963.
rules.start_event: Date of the judgment or order sought to be appealed from
rules.notes: Where the High Court refused a certificate, use the 60-day rule from the order of refusal.

rules.title: Special leave petition (civil) after the High Court refused a certificate
rules.basis: Article 133 of the Schedule to the Limitation Act, 1963 (clause (b)): special leave to appeal to the Supreme Court where leave to appeal was refused by the High Court, sixty days from the date of the order of refusal. Order XXI Rule 1 of the Supreme Court Rules, 2013. Articles 134A and 136 of the Constitution of India. Computed under Sections 4, 5 and 12 of the Limitation Act, 1963.
rules.start_event: Date of the High Court's order refusing the certificate
rules.notes: Whether an oral refusal starts this period is unsettled: if in doubt, also compute the 90-day rule from the judgment and keep the earlier date.

rules.title: Application to set aside an arbitral award (s. 34)
rules.basis: Section 34(3) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996: three months from the date the applicant received the arbitral award (or from the disposal of a request under Section 33 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996); under the proviso the court may entertain it within a further thirty days on sufficient cause, but not thereafter. Section 43(1) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 applies the Limitation Act, 1963; Section 4 of the Limitation Act, 1963 applies to the three months only, and Section 29(2) of the Limitation Act, 1963 excludes Section 5.
rules.remedy: Petition to set aside an arbitral award
rules.forum: Court as defined in Section 2(1)(e) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996
rules.start_event: Date the applicant received the signed arbitral award (or the disposal of a Section 33 request)

outer_limit.label: End of the 30 days the court may allow on sufficient cause (proviso to s. 34(3)); no further extension
outer_limit.basis: Proviso to Section 34(3) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996

rules.notes: s. 4 extends only the three-month period; the 30 days run from the end of the three months, not from a later reopening day. The Supreme Court's COVID order also covered outer limits within which delay can be condoned.

rules.title: Written statement in a commercial suit
rules.basis: Order VIII Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (proviso), as amended for commercial disputes by Section 16 of the Commercial Courts Act, 2015 and its Schedule: thirty days from service of summons, which the court may extend for reasons recorded and on costs to not later than one hundred and twenty days from service, after which the defendant forfeits the right to file it. Section 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

outer_limit.label: Day 120 from service: the court cannot take the written statement on record after this
outer_limit.basis: Order VIII Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (proviso), as amended by the Commercial Courts Act, 2015

rules.notes: Not a Limitation Act period: whether a closed last day carries over (s. 10 of the General Clauses Act) is uncertain, so any shift is shown for information and the docket keeps the unshifted date.

rules.title: Written statement in an ordinary civil suit
rules.basis: Order VIII Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908: thirty days from service of summons; the court may allow a later date, not later than ninety days from service, for reasons recorded in writing. Section 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

outer_limit.label: Day 90 from service: the period the court may allow; for ordinary suits it is directory, so a later filing needs the court's leave
outer_limit.basis: Order VIII Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908

rules.notes: Not a Limitation Act period: a closed last day is shown for information and the docket keeps the unshifted date.

rules.title: Execution of a decree or order of a civil court
rules.basis: Article 136 of the Schedule to the Limitation Act, 1963: execution of any decree (other than a decree granting a mandatory injunction) or order of any civil court, twelve years from when the decree or order becomes enforceable; a decree granting a perpetual injunction is not subject to any period of limitation. Section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1963 does not apply to applications under Order XXI of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. Computed under Sections 4 and 14 of the Limitation Act, 1963.
rules.start_event: Date the decree or order became enforceable (or the default in a payment or delivery it directs)
rules.notes: Delay cannot be condoned under s. 5. Decrees granting a mandatory injunction are under Article 135 (three years) and are not covered.
